title: The Efficacy and Safety of Dalfampridine on Cognition and Fatigue in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Halabi MH, Alromayan R, Almutairi M, Alasmari H, AlGhamdi MA, Makkawi S
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting the central nervous system. People with MS frequently experience cognitive dysfunction and fatigue. Dalfampridine (DAL), a potassium channel blocker, is US Food and Drug Administration-approved for the treatment of walking impairment in people with MS. It may also enhance nerve conduction in regions associated with fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. This study aims to evaluate DAL's efficacy in improving these symptoms, as well as its safety profile, in people with MS. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science, covering all records from database inception through April 1, 2024. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing DAL with placebo in people with MS and reporting impaired cognition and fatigue were included. A random-effects model was used to calculate the risk ratio (RR), standardized mean difference (SMD), and mean difference (MD) with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Of 1329 studies identified, 13 RCTs involving a total of 827 people with MS were included. DAL demonstrated a significant improvement in cognitive symptoms (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI, 0.04-0.38; P = .01; I² = 6%). However, no significant difference was observed between DAL and placebo in reducing fatigue (MD = 3.70; 95% CI, -4.37 to 11.77;P = .37; I² = 19%). Safety measures were comparable, with no significant difference in adverse events (RR = 1.11; 95% CI, 0.99-1.25; P = .08; I² = 0%). CONCLUSIONS: People with MS receiving DAL demonstrated significant improvement in cognitive symptoms; however, further studies are warranted to validate and confirm this finding.

title: Effect of electroconvulsive therapy on anhedonia in adults with major depressive disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Radmard R, Panganiban KJ, Kwan ATH, Dri CE, Guillen-Burgos HF, van Bruggen FH, Bargiota SI, Ho R
abstract: BACKGROUND: Anhedonia is a core symptom of major depressive disorder (MDD) and may persist despite otherwise effective treatment. Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a widely used and effective intervention for severe and treatment-resistant depression, however, its specific effects on anhedonia remain poorly characterized. OBJECTIVE: To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis examining ECT-associated changes in anhedonia in adults with MDD. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across Embase, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Scopus. Studies were eligible if they included adults with MDD, administered ECT as a treatment, and assessed anhedonia using a validated scale. Standardized mean change ratios (SMCs) were calculated and pooled using a random-effects model. RESULTS: Eleven studies were included in the systematic review, of which five provided quantitative data for meta-analysis. Across 132 participants, ECT was associated with a significant improvement in anhedonia severity (SMC = 1.02; 95% CI, 0.63-1.42). CONCLUSIONS: ECT was associated with a statistically significant improvement in anhedonia among adults with MDD. However, given the small number of included studies and non-randomized pre-post designs, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Future ECT studies should assess anhedonia as an outcome, while using a validated anhedonia measure.

title: Prospective Multicenter Evaluation of a Novel Low-Axial-Force Colonic Stent for Malignant Colorectal Obstruction.
authors: Otsuka R, Saito S, Fujimoto N, Hanabata N, Takao A, Narita K, Kuwai T, Endo S
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Self-expandable metal stents (SEMSs) are used as a bridge to surgery (BTS) or for palliation (PAL) in malignant colorectal obstruction, but high axial force may contribute to perforation. We prospectively evaluated the efficacy and safety of the low-axial-force Naturfit colonic stent in both settings. METHODS: This prospective multicenter single-arm study enrolled 208 patients at 11 Japanese institutions between 2019 and 2022 (BTS, n = 137; PAL, n = 71). The primary endpoint was clinical success of colorectal stenting; secondary endpoints included technical success, adverse events, surgical outcomes after BTS stenting, and 12-month palliative outcomes. RESULTS: Technical success and clinical success of colorectal stenting were both 99.0%, with perforation in three patients (1.4%). In the BTS cohort, clinical success of BTS was 97.1%; no perforations occurred, and early and late adverse-event rates were 1.5% and 3.7%. All patients underwent elective surgery; colostomy and laparoscopic surgery rates were 4.4% and 87.6%. In the palliative cohort, clinical success of colorectal stenting was 98.6%, late adverse events occurred in 16.9%, and 12-month overall survival and stent patency were 46.6% and 67.6%. CONCLUSIONS: Naturfit achieved high technical and clinical success of colorectal stenting with a low perforation rate. These findings support its feasibility for malignant colorectal obstruction in both BTS and palliative settings, although comparative studies are needed to determine relative advantages over other SEMSs. TRIAL REGISTRATION: University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trial Registry: UMIN000035224.

title: Engineering copper homeostasis for microenvironment-adaptive therapy in inflammation-driven disorders.
authors: Ding F, Liu J, Liu M, Huang H, Tang H, Zhong J, Liu C, Liu Z
abstract: Inflammation-driven disorders (IDDs) arise from distinct initiating events, yet many persist because immune activation, oxidative and metabolic stress, regulated cell death, and tissue remodeling form self-reinforcing local niches. Copper connects these processes through its roles as a cuproenzyme cofactor, redox-active species and dynamically trafficked regulatory metal. Its therapeutic significance, however, is determined by disease stage, cell type, subcellular distribution and chemical state. Copper deficiency, excess or mislocalization may therefore be adaptive, protective or pathogenic in different contexts. This review develops a disease- and copper-state-specific framework that links copper homeostasis to therapeutic platform design. We first examine inflammation-associated remodeling of copper trafficking and compare representative copper states in autoimmune joint disease, metabolic inflammation, fibrosis, inflammation-associated cancer and infection-associated tissue repair. We then critically evaluate copper-dependent and copper-sensitive mechanisms governing inflammatory mediator availability, immune-cell programming and checkpoint regulation, regulated cell death, angiogenesis and stromal remodeling, while distinguishing direct mechanistic evidence from model-dependent inference. Building on this analysis, we compare pharmacological modulators with nanocarriers, copper-containing active materials and local copper-sequestering platforms that implement copper chelation or sequestration, controlled copper delivery or release, intracellular redistribution, and catalytic activation or nanozyme-like redox regulation. We further outline how pathological copper pools, activation cues, release kinetics, speciation, biodistribution and target engagement should be measured so that precision is demonstrated rather than inferred from material composition. This framework positions copper modulation as a context-specific complement to existing therapy and defines the mechanistic, analytical and translational evidence required for microenvironment-adaptive treatment of IDDs.

title: Care of Special Populations in Disasters.
authors: Kirkpatrick S, Khan U
journal: The Surgical clinics of North America
abstract: Disasters and mass casualty incidents disproportionately harm elderly, pediatric, and pregnant patients, yet most triage algorithms and preparedness plans are built around the healthy adult. This review examines the physiologic, anatomic, and social characteristics that make each population vulnerable, drawing on experience from Hurricane Katrina and contemporary armed conflict. For older adults, frailty, rather than chronologic age, drives outcomes, and polypharmacy complicates resuscitation. Children require age-adjusted triage, weight-based dosing, and protection from family separation. Pregnant patients require simultaneous maternal and fetal assessment, as the physiologic adaptations of pregnancy mask hemorrhage. Systems-level preparedness remains the strongest determinant of outcome.

title: A let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicle-laden bioactive scaffold promotes immunomodulation and regeneration of segmental tracheal defects.
authors: Liu B, Wei N, Liang L, Shi Z, Liu P, Zeng T, Zhang H, Zhang H
abstract: Segmental tracheal defects resulting from trauma, tumor resection, or congenital malformations pose significant challenges for reconstruction. Persistent post-injury inflammation, inadequate neovascularization, and delayed epithelial restoration contribute to the formation of granulation tissue and subsequent graft failure. In this study, we developed a bioactive tracheal scaffold for sustained local delivery of let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicles (let-7a-5p-EVs) to modulate the regenerative microenvironment during tracheal repair. The scaffold was constructed by integrating a mechanically optimized polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a 20% Pluronic F127 hydrogel, which served as a local reservoir for EV retention and sustained release. Let-7a-5p-EVs were generated from lentivirally engineered human gingiva-derived mesenchymal stem cells and showed typical EV morphology, representative EV marker expression, and efficient uptake by airway epithelial cells. In vitro, let-7a-5p-EVs enhanced airway epithelial cell migration and shifted lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophages from a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype toward a reparative M2-like phenotype, accompanied by reduced inflammatory cytokine expression. In a rabbit segmental tracheal defect model, the let-7a-5p-EV-laden scaffold enhanced neovascularization, mitigated local inflammatory responses, promoted mucociliary epithelial reconstruction, and maintained airway patency. The let-7a-5p-EV scaffold improved biomechanical recovery, and increased survival rates. Transcriptomic profiling and molecular validation indicated that these effects were associated with the attenuation of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)-associated inflammatory activation, as evidenced by reduced p65 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. These findings demonstrate that sustained local delivery of engineered EVs from a mechanically competent bioactive scaffold provides an effective immunomodulatory strategy for the regenerative repair of segmental tracheal defects and offers translational potential for functional airway reconstruction.

title: Transrectal ultrasonographic assessment of the equine fetal distal limb beyond the first phalanx for predicting fetal age and bone development in Quarter Horses.
authors: Renaudin C, Wensley F, Morgan J, Cassano J, Spriet M
abstract: In Quarter Horses (QH), fetal age can be predicted within 2 weeks prior to 200- days of gestation ultrasonographically; however, as pregnancy advances, accuracy decreases. Recently, fetal ultrasonographic measurement of the first phalanx length (P1L) was introduced as a novel biometric parameter during late gestation, and the timing of appearance and closure of P1 epiphyses has been identified as potential markers of bone development. The overall aim of this study is to describe distal limb bone development beyond the first phalanx. Ten healthy pregnant mares (9 QH and 1 Thoroughbred carrying a QH fetus) with known ovulation dates were used. Transrectal ultrasonography was performed every 2 weeks from 9 months of gestation until parturition. P2 length (P2L) correlated highly with days of gestation (p < 0.0001; r2 = 0.75). A correlation equation was established: y = 5.343 (±0.403) x +205.1(±6.99) (y = predicted value of gestational age in days; x = P2 length in mm). Ossification of distal MC3, P1 and P2 epiphyses, and sesamoid bones, appeared in a chronological order, with the distal MC3 epiphysis ossification center appearing first, followed by distal P1, distal P2, proximal sesamoid bones, and finally distal sesamoid bone. Distal limb ossification can be considered complete in QH when the distal MC3 epiphysis, proximal epiphyses of P1 and P2, and all sesamoid bones are present. Clinically, fetal ultrasonography of the distal limb may be used to assess fetal age and bone development.

title: Sustained delivery of 3D-bioprinted stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles promotes neural regeneration following traumatic brain injury via the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 axis.
authors: Ai Y, Zhang Q, Chen T, Lin L, Chen Z, Liu G, Liu J, Dong Z
abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical translation of stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) for traumatic brain injury (TBI) is restricted by low yield in 2D culture and rapid in vivo clearance. OBJECTIVE: To develop an in situ sustained delivery system (3D-sEVs@Gel) encapsulating 3D-bioprinted adipose stem cell (ADSC)-derived sEVs (3D-ADSC-sEVs) within GelMA (Gelatin methacryloyl) hydrogel for long-term functional repair after TBI. METHODS: SEVs derived from coaxially bioprinted 3D-ADSCs were isolated, and a GelMA hydrogel-based delivery system was subsequently constructed. Following orthotopic transplantation of the 3D-sEVs@Gel system into the lesion site after TBI, functional recovery, neural stem cell (NSC) proliferation and lineage-associated responses, and the underlying molecular mechanisms were systematically evaluated through behavioral tests, immunofluorescence, multi-omics, and pharmacological inhibition. RESULTS: SEVs generated using the coaxial alginate-microfiber culture system exhibited an approximately eightfold higher yields and protein loading compared with those obtained from 2D culture. In vivo, 3D-sEVs@Gel prolonged local retention, reduced tissue loss, and significantly improved long-term sensorimotor coordination and spatial memory following TBI. In addition, treatment increased the numbers of proliferating cells co-expressing neural progenitor-, neuronal-, and oligodendroglial-lineage-associated markers within the examined neurogenic regions. Mechanistically, 3D-sEV treatment increased nuclear CREB1 levels in NSCs, promoting PGC-1α transcription and subsequent FNDC5 expression, thereby supporting endogenous neurogenesis and functional neural repair. CONCLUSION: The 3D-sEVs@Gel system promotes chronic neurological reconstruction post-TBI by modulating NSC proliferation and neural lineage-associated responses through the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 pathway, offering a promising cell-free strategy for neural repair and tissue engineering.

title: Long-term Endoscopic Evolution of a Pyloric Gland Adenoma Arising in Nonatrophic Gastric Mucosa and Initially Resembling a Fundic Gland Polyp.
authors: Kobayashi R, Nakanishi H, Takaura K, Tanaka S, Maeyashiki C, Tamaki N, Yasui Y, Sakurai U
abstract: Pyloric gland adenoma (PGA) is a rare gastric epithelial neoplasm often associated with autoimmune or metaplastic atrophic gastritis. An 80-year-old man underwent serial upper gastrointestinal endoscopy. A small gastric fundus lesion initially resembling a fundic gland polyp (FGP) was followed without biopsy. Over 11 years, it enlarged to 22 mm and became increasingly whitish, against a background described endoscopically as nonatrophic. Biopsy suggested PGA, and the lesion was resected en bloc by endoscopic submucosal dissection. Closely packed pyloric-type glands showed elongation, tortuosity, branching, and cystic dilatation, with diffuse MUC6 expression and MUC5AC expression restricted to the surface epithelium. The lesion was diagnosed as PGA with low-grade dysplasia. The adjacent oxyntic mucosa showed no atrophy, lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, or nodular enterochromaffin-like cell hyperplasia. Without an initial biopsy, whether the lesion was already PGA or developed within a pre-existing FGP remains unknown. An enlarging or increasingly whitish FGP-like lesion warrants histologic assessment, even in nonatrophic gastric mucosa.

title: Hybrid nanovesicle artificial antigen-presenting cells integrate endogenous tumor antigen display with senescence-mimetic erythrocyte membrane-directed splenic T-cell priming.
authors: Yang Z, Li S, Guo Y, Wang T, Han H, Ma M, Zhang Y, Tang W
abstract: Artificial antigen-presenting cells (aAPCs) provide a non-genetic approach to T-cell activation, but their in vivo performance is often limited by predefined peptide-major histocompatibility complex class I (pMHC-I) repertoires and inefficient delivery to secondary lymphoid organs. Here, we engineer senescence-derived hybrid nanovesicles that integrate endogenous antigen display and organ-directed trafficking within a single membrane material. Nanovesicles derived from senescent cancer cells retain increased levels of endogenously generated pMHC-I complexes, whereas nanovesicles derived from senescence-mimetic red blood cells confer spleen-directed biodistribution. Fusion of these membranes generates SS-hNVs, which are further functionalized with anti-CD28 and interleukin-2 to form SS-aAPCs that provide coordinated T-cell receptor (TCR), costimulatory, and cytokine signals. Hybrid membrane composition governs splenic accumulation and CD8+ T-cell engagement following intravenous administration. SS-aAPCs expand antigen-specific CD8+ T cells and TCF-1+PD-1+ progenitor-like populations, enhance cytotoxic responses, and suppress tumor growth in B16-OVA and MC38 models. Combination with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) blockade further improves tumor control. By assigning endogenous antigen display and lymphoid trafficking to distinct source membranes, this platform establishes a structure-function strategy for constructing systemically administered aAPCs. These findings support that physiologically remodeled membranes can be assembled as modular biomaterials to coordinate molecular immune signaling with organ-level biodistribution, enabling in vivo T-cell priming without predefined epitope loading or genetic modification of immune cells.

title: Lightweight interpretable support vector machine SERS (LiSVM-SERS) learning framework for serological diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis and biomarker identification.
authors: Zhang H, Lin W, Pan H, Cao L, Wang Y, Sun H, Zhao Y, Jia Y
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA), a chronic, autoimmune form of arthritis that causes joint inflammation and occurs with the skin condition psoriasis, is difficult to clinically diagnose at an early stage due to insignificant symptoms and lack of biomarkers. Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) is a powerful tool to identify specific biomolecules for liquid biopsy. Here, we establish a lightweight interpretable support vector machine SERS (LiSVM-SERS) learning framework for serological diagnosis of PsA and identification of potential biomarkers. The fs-laser-nanofabricated Au@mica SERS substrates with a relative standard deviation of 8.80% in intensity homogeneity are employed to obtain reliable serum Raman spectra. The SVM algorithm is performed to train the machine-learning model for PsA classification using only 26 samples (PsA = 13 and healthy controls = 13). The hyperplane coefficient vectors from the trained SVM model are then employed as the filtered weights of Raman shifts, followed by logistic-probability mapping and Welch's t-test to filter highly-significant spectral features, identifying 432 most-significant Raman shifts for 7 potential biomarkers. The trained LiSVM-SERS model demonstrates the outstanding sensitivity and specificity of 98.0% and 96.0%, respectively, validated by an internal independent blind-test cohort (PsA = 30, healthy controls = 30) and a cross disease-control cohort (systemic lupus erythematosus = 15, rheumatoid arthritis = 15, and osteoarthritis = 15). The present work not only provides a simple and lightweight non-invasive technique to diagnose PsA, but also paves a new way to identify the potential biomarkers from the label-free serum SERS spectra for autoimmune disorders.

title: Young children engage in choice-relative moral reasoning.
authors: Waltzer T, Heyman GD, Leslie AM, Levine S
abstract: A central challenge in moral reasoning is evaluating actions not only by their outcomes, but also by the alternatives that were available at the time of choice. The present study examined whether preschool-age children engage in this form of choice-relative moral reasoning. Using a child-friendly version of the trolley problem, 3- to 5-year-old children (N = 124, 51% girls) judged a protagonist who moved a barrier to protect three children's cookies from being eaten by a mean squirrel. Children typically judged this action as morally good when no better alternative was available, even when it caused harm to another child. However, they judged the same action as morally bad when a non-harmful alternative was available but not chosen. These findings suggest that preschool-age children evaluate actions in light of available alternatives rather than solely on the basis of outcomes. Thus, even young children appear to consider what else could have been done when making moral judgments.

title: Do parental questions and gestures support executive functions in toddlers born preterm and full-term?
authors: Yılmaz B, Göksun T
abstract: This study examined parental questions and gestures in the development of executive functions (EF) in preterm (PT) and full-term (FT) toddlers. Sixty-four Turkish-speaking parent-child dyads (32 girls, Mage = 26.1 months, SD = 1.33, 25 PT) were observed in free-play sessions. The form (i.e., WH, yes/no) and function (i.e., pedagogical, information-seeking, rhetorical) of parental questions and gestures accompanying them were coded. Children's working memory and cognitive flexibility skills were measured using Hide the Pots and Reverse Categorization (pre- and post-switch) tasks, respectively. Results showed that PT and FT children had similar EF skills. Parental WH questions were associated with PT children's working memory skills. Parental WH questions, not pedagogical ones, were related to children's cognitive flexibility skills, regardless of neonatal status. When accompanied by gestures, both WH and pedagogical questions were associated with PT children's working memory and cognitive flexibility skills. These results highlight the importance of specific parental input as a function of children's neonatal status in the development of EFs.

title: Early self-regulation in context: Multidimensional organization of neonatal non-nutritive sucking and its association with subclinical maternal depressive traits.
authors: Faré O, Silvestri V, Morniroli D, Petrelli A, Colombo L, Giannì ML, Bulf H
abstract: From the very first days of life, infants' affective regulation unfolds within a dyadic co-regulatory system shaped by caregiver responsivity. In contexts of reduced maternal availability, such as maternal depressive states, infants may be required to compensate for diminished interpersonal regulation by increasingly relying on their internal resources. Neonatal non-nutritive sucking (NNS) represents one of the earliest spontaneously available regulatory behaviors, contributing to physiological and behavioral homeostasis from birth. However, it remains unclear whether its spontaneous organization is associated with early relational vulnerability indexed by maternal depressive symptoms. The present study aimed to characterize the spontaneous organization of NNS in a sample of newborns (N = 42) and to examine whether individual differences in NNS are associated with maternal postnatal depressive subclinical traits measured using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). Results from an exploratory principal component analysis indicated that neonatal sucking behavior was organized along two functional dimensions, reflecting overall sucking effort and behavioral activation, and the temporal organization of sucking bursts. Importantly, higher maternal depressive traits, though subclinical, were selectively associated with increased sucking effort, with infants of mothers reporting higher depressive traits showing more frequent and intense sucking, while no differences emerged for the organizational dimension. Overall, these findings suggest that individual differences in maternal depressive traits within the subclinical range may be associated with neonatal NNS effort, a precocious compensatory mobilization of regulatory resources, potentially serving both to support autonomous regulation and to elicit maternal engagement.

title: Accuracy of parent and teacher reports of early math skills.
authors: King YA, Zippert EL, Ellis A, O'Rear C, Lin J, Purpura DJ
abstract: BACKGROUND: It is important for parents and teachers to understand preschooler's early mathematics skills to best provide appropriate mathematics support. Comparing parents' and teachers' accuracy in reporting children's mathematics skills may help to ensure developmentally appropriate early math support in home and classroom environments. AIM: The present study examined the accuracy of parents' and teachers' reports of preschoolers' early mathematics skills (i.e., counting, numeral identification, and quantitative and spatial word knowledge). SAMPLE: Participants included 117 children 3 to 5 years old (M = 4.27, SD = .63, 49.6 % female) and their parent and Head Start teacher. METHOD: Parents and teachers completed surveys reporting on each child's understanding of mathematics concepts via items from different mathematics measures. Children were directly assessed on their mathematics skills via the same or similar items. RESULTS: Generally, parents' and teachers' reports were positively associated with direct assessments of children's mathematics skills. Parents' and teachers' reports of children's mathematical skills ranged from 47 % to 75 % accurate, and parents were more accurate than teachers in reporting children's quantitative word knowledge. The direction of inaccuracies (over-or underestimation) varied by mathematics skill type, such that caregivers tended to overestimate children's numeracy skills and underestimate their mathematical language knowledge. CONCLUSION: Future research is needed to examine how the accuracy of parents and teachers reports influences early mathematics development, and how potentially improving caregiver accuracy might support children's mathematics learning.

title: Parent-child facial expression recognition: the role of familiarity in interactive contexts.
authors: Palmer K, Buttle HM, Kohler M, Fong FTK, Nelson NL
abstract: The ability to express and understand emotion is fundamental to social communication, and develops through early parent-child interactions. Across two studies, we examined parents' and children's recognition of emotional expressions during a structured interactive task. In Study 1, parent-child dyads (N = 33, children aged 4-9 years) took turns producing facial expressions in response to emotion-eliciting objects while their partner guessed the eliciting object. Videos of children were shown to naïve adult raters (N = 88) completing the same task. Study 1 provided initial evidence for a familiarity effect, with parents outperforming naïve raters at recognising their child's expressions. Study 2 (N = 45 dyads, children aged 4-12 years) extended this by testing whether recognition accuracy reflects familiarity with a specific partner or general parenting experience. Participants completed the task with each other and with videos of unfamiliar partners. Naïve parents (N = 69) and non-parents (N = 68) also rated the children's expressions. Study 2 confirmed a bidirectional familiarity advantage: both parents and children were more accurate with their familiar partner than with unfamiliar individuals, suggesting the effect is specific to the parent-child relationship rather than reflecting a general ability to read adult or child faces. Recognition accuracy was not strongly predicted by age, suggesting familiarity may account for more variance in performance than developmental changes in expressive clarity alone. These findings support the view that the unique parent-child bond plays a meaningful role in emotional understanding.

title: Dual-mode colorimetric sensing of bilirubin using a PDDA@peroxomolybdate composite: A spectrophotometric platform and cost-effective cotton-swab sensor for point-of-care testing.
authors: Avan AA, Filik H, Kucur M, Cabıoğlu N
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: In this work, the synthesis and characterization of a poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA)@peroxomolybdate composite are presented for the development of a dual-mode colorimetric sensing platform for point-of-care bilirubin (BLR) detection. The platform combines a laboratory-based spectrophotometric assay with a smartphone-assisted cotton-swab sensor, enabling versatile and accessible screening. The spectrophotometric mode exhibited a wide linear detection range of 0.1-4.5 mg/dL (1.72-77.0 μM) and a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.032 mg/dL (0.54 μM). In parallel, the smartphone-based assay, utilizing normalized red-channel intensity values, demonstrated a broader linear range of 0.1-9.0 mg/dL (1.72-154 μM) with an LOD of 0.046 mg/dL (0.78 μM). This dual-mode sensing approach offers flexibility by letting users choose between the high analytical accuracy of laboratory instrumentation and the convenience of wide-range, on-site screening, depending on clinical requirements. Furthermore, the selectivity of the platform was comprehensively evaluated, and its practical applicability was successfully validated using adult and neonatal blood serum samples. The results highlight the strong potential of the proposed platform for reliable clinical monitoring of BLR levels.

Integrated serum pharmacochemistry , network pharmacology, untargeted metabolomics and experimental validation to explore the mechanism of Wenjian Qigong Decoction in the treatment of polycystic ovary syndrome.
authors: Wang X, Liu C, Zhang Z, Huang Y, Liu Z, Song Y, Hu R, Ma W
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a prevalent endocrine and metabolic disorder among women of reproductive age, currently has no definitive treatment. Qigong Wan (QGW), first documented in Yifang Jijie, is a classic prescription for infertility in obese women. Given the heterogeneous and complex nature of PCOS, Wenjian Qigong Decoction (WJQG), a modified formula derived from QGW that incorporates medicinal ingredients from Jiawei Buzhong Yiqi Decoction (JWBZYQ), Guishen Wan (GSW), and Jiaotai Wan (JTW), exhibits remarkable therapeutic efficacy for obese PCOS in clinical practice. The efficacy of all constituent herbs in WJQG has been confirmed, whereas its pharmacological mechanisms remain to be clarified. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the potential therapeutic benefits of WJQG for the treatment of PCOS and provide mechanistic insights into its mode of action. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An obese PCOS rat model was established via testosterone propionate (TP) injection combined with a 45% high-fat diet (HFD). The therapeutic efficacy of WJQG, as well as the validity of the model, was evaluated by assessing body weight, visceral fat content, estrous cycle, clinical chemistry indicators, and histopathology. Furthermore, a comprehensive approach integrating ovarian untargeted metabolomics, serum pharmacochemistry , network pharmacology, molecular docking, and experimental validation was employed to systematically elucidate the potential mechanism of action of WJQG in treating obese PCOS. RESULTS: WJQG significantly attenuated body weight gain, reduced abdominal visceral fat, restored estrous cyclicity, improved ovarian morphology, and corrected hyperandrogenemia and endocrine dysregulation in obese PCOS rats. Serum pharmacochemistry identified 22 bioactive prototype compounds absorbed into the blood. Network pharmacology predicted hub targets including TNF, IL6, CASP3, and PTGS2. Subsequent molecular docking simulations indicated favorable binding affinities between these proteins and representative prototype constituents such as narirutin, ginsenoside Rc, and hyperoside. Untargeted metabolomics suggested that WJQG substantially remodeled the ovarian metabolome, specifically suppressing the hyperactivated arachidonic acid metabolism pathway and downregulating downstream pro-inflammatory lipid mediators (PGF2α, PGA2, PGE2, and 10,11-dihydro-20-hydroxy-LTB4). Mechanistically, WJQG inhibited the enzymatic cascade of p-cPLA2, COX-2 (encoded by PTGS2), and 5-LOX. Meanwhile, WJQG treatment was associated with restored ADPN/PPARα/p-AMPK signaling, a predominance of M2-type macrophages, a suppressed NLRP3/NF-κB inflammatory cascade accompanied by reduced TNF-α and IL-6 levels, and alleviated granulosa-cell apoptosis alongside decreased caspase-3 activation. CONCLUSIONS: WJQG alleviates key disease manifestations in obese PCOS rats, which correlates with modulation of the interconnected pathological triad of intra-ovarian arachidonic acid metabolism hyperactivation, chronic inflammation, and granulosa-cell apoptosis. These findings provide supportive scientific evidence and pharmacodynamic rationale to support further pre-clinical investigation of WJQG as a potential integrative therapeutic candidate for PCOS.

title: SVIP knockdown alters UPS protein expression in human testicular embryonal carcinoma cells.
authors: Kipel Ş, Çayli S, Aktaş Gİ, Nakkaş H
abstract: Testicular tumours are the most common malignant tumors in men between the ages of 15-34. Approximately 95% of testicular tumors arise from germ cells. Small VCP-interacting protein (SVIP) is a protein that regulates its function and autophagy by binding to p97/VCP, which is involved in protein degradation associated with the endoplasmic reticulum. Recent studies on SVIP have shown that SVIP is an androgen-sensitive protein. The development of secondary sex characteristics is influenced by androgens, which are significant steroid hormone. Androgens also initiate and maintain spermatogenesis in the male reproductive system. Mutations of androgen receptors are often seen in patients with disorders of male reproductive development and can cause male infertility. Studies are showing that the ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS) in the male reproductive system affects fertility. Therefore, investigating the expressions of USP26 and UXT, which are components of the UPS, is important for testicular biology. The expressions of SVIP, AR, Ubiquitin, USP26 and UXT were analysed by immunofluorescence, western blot and q RT-PCR method to determine the expressions of SVIP and the UPS proteins that it interacts in human testicular embryonal carcinoma cells (CRL-2073) and to see the effects of suppressed SVIP expression on other proteins after SVIP siRNA transfection. At SVIP siRNA applied CRL-2073 cells, SVIP, AR, USP26 and Ubiquitin expressions decreased, while UXT expression increased, according to immunofluorescence and western blot results. According to the qRT-PCR results, SVIP gene expression decreased and AR, Ubiquitin, USP26 and UXT gene expressions increased in the group given SVIP siRNA. As a result, this study demonstrated the expression of SVIP and its interacting UPS proteins in CRL-2073 cells for the first time, making an unique and significant contribution to the literature.

title: Clinical characteristics and maternal whole-exome sequencing findings in patients with recurrent oocyte, zygote, and early embryo maturation arrest: a single-center experience.
authors: Kahraman S, Cetinkaya M, Cetinkaya CP, Madjunkova S, Kara B, Ayaz A, Aktoz F
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To characterize the clinical phenotype, cumulative assisted reproductive technology (ART) experience, and maternal whole-exome sequencing (WES) findings in patients with recurrent Oocyte, Zygote, and Early Embryo Maturation Arrest (OZEMA), and to assess the contribution of phenotype-guided genomic evaluation in this clinically challenging population. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study conducted in a fertility clinic within a general private hospital equipped with an in‑house genetic laboratory. SUBJECTS: A total of 115 females with a history of OZEMA were included, all of whom presented to the ART clinic. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The distribution of pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in established OZEMA-associated genes, variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in established genes, monoallelic variants in established autosomal recessive genes, and exploratory candidate-gene findings. ART outcomes were described according to whether a prioritized WES finding was reported. RESULTS: The mean female age was 33.47 +/- 4.37 years, with a median infertility duration of 6.0 years (range, 1.0-21.0). Patients had experienced recurrent OZEMA across multiple ART cycles (median, 4; range, 1-16). Parental consanguinity was observed in 37 of 115 cases (32.2 %). Prioritized maternal WES findings were identified in 64 of 115 patients (55.7 %): 12 patients (10.4 %) had P/LP variants in established genes with genotypes consistent with the reported inheritance pattern, 17 (14.8 %) had VUS in established genes, 15 (13.0 %) had monoallelic variants in established autosomal recessive genes without a second relevant allele, and 20 (17.4 %) had exploratory candidate-gene findings. No prioritized WES finding was identified in 51 patients (44.3 %). CONCLUSIONS: Phenotype-guided maternal WES identified established P/LP findings with inheritance-consistent support in a clinically meaningful subset of patients with recurrent OZEMA and revealed a broader spectrum of additional genomic findings. These results support genomic evaluation, while the clinical interpretation of VUS, monoallelic findings in recessive genes, and exploratory candidate-gene findings should remain evidence-based.

title: Duration of post-ovulation uterine fluid in mares with persistent mating-induced endometritis predicts pregnancy rate, and earlier mating shifts fluid persistence relative to ovulation.
authors: England GCW, Newcombe JR
abstract: Persistent mating-induced endometritis commonly causes subfertility in mares. We assessed 313 natural-cover breeding cycles from 192 mares examined daily until at least day 5 after ovulation, establishing the last day post-ovulation on which uterine fluid remained detectable. Fluid was detected after ovulation in 52.4% of all cycles. The longer fluid persisted the lower the pregnancy rate: 73.8% with no post-ovulation fluid, 32.0% when fluid was last detected on day 2 post-ovulation, and 17.6% when fluid persisted to day 3 or beyond. Each additional day fluid persisted post-ovulation was associated with a 41% reduction in the odds of pregnancy. Recording fluid duration relative to ovulation was superior in predicting pregnancy compared with recording fluid duration relative to mating. Data from a subsequent cycle were available for 101 mares bred again at cycle 2 (97 that did not conceive at cycle 1 and 4 that had lost a cycle 1 pregnancy); attempts were made to mate the mare earlier in subsequent cycles. Total number of days fluid was detectable from mating was similar at cycle 1 and cycle 2 in these mares (1.88 versus 1.86 days; P = 0.77). In 54 mares the day of mating at the next cycle relative to ovulation was advanced by at least one day at cycle 2; and yet the duration of fluid persistence remained unchanged. Consequently, the last day of fluid persistence post-ovulation decreased (1.61 to 0.65 days; P < 0.001). In the 47 mares whose mating interval was unchanged at cycle 2, the last post-ovulation fluid day was also unchanged, providing an internal control for the redistribution finding. Earlier mating was associated with higher pregnancy rates across all cycles (OR 1.969; P < 0.001) but not significantly when only first-cycles were analysed (P = 0.92), or after adjustment for cycle number (P = 0.69). Persistence of fluid post-ovulation is negatively associated with pregnancy rate, with a critical reduction when fluid persists beyond day 2. In treated mares, total fluid duration appeared to be a fixed characteristic; earlier mating redistributed the period of fluid persistence to earlier relative to ovulation, resulting in fewer post-ovulation fluid days. Plausibly, earlier fluid resolution after ovulation may allow better uterine recovery prior to entry of the embryo and thus increase pregnancy rate.

title: Hemodynamic effects of ventilating or not, during cardiopulmonary bypass in a porcine model.
authors: Kvalheim VL, Mongstad A, Husby P, Stangeland L, Nginamau ES, Osman TA, Yamada S, Grong K
abstract: Background. Optimal ventilator setting during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is unknown. Improved gas exchange and lung compliance have been suggested as favourable outcomes when lungs are ventilated. However, long-time effects have been hard to demonstrate. There has been less focus on the immediate circulatory effects of ventilator settings during cardioplegia and CPB, and potentially hemodynamic effects of different ventilator strategies are unknown. Methods. Sixteen anesthetized pigs on normothermic CPB with 80 min of aortic cross-clamp and cardioplegic arrest were randomized to a ventilated and a not ventilated group. After weaning, both cardiac-, hemodynamic-, and pulmonary functions were evaluated for up to 120 min. Results. Left ventricular variables and cardiac output did not differ between the two study groups, neither before nor after weaning. After weaning, mean pulmonary artery pressure was increased in ventilated compared to not ventilated animals. Neither pulmonary compliance nor oxygen uptake differed between groups in surviving animals. Conclusions. Disconnection of the ventilator during CPB and cardiac arrest did not affect lung compliance and oxygen uptake, neither positively nor negatively. In the ventilated group, a temporary increase in the pulmonary pressure after weaning was observed.

title: An optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched dual-crosslinkable hydrogel for cell-free remodeling of the corneal stroma.
authors: Wu W, Huai S, Li C, Wang L, Xie S, Lei L, Liu X, Wang J
abstract: Corneal trauma is a leading cause of visual impairment and blindness worldwide, yet corneal stromal repair and regeneration remain a significant challenge in ophthalmology because of its limited intrinsic repair capacity and fibrotic scar formation during healing process. Here we report an optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched in situ dual-crosslinkable hydrogel that enables cell-free corneal stromal remodeling. By integrating dynamic covalent crosslinking with static photocrosslinking strategy, the optimized hydrogel-based substitute achieved high optical transparency, a refractive index of approximately 1.35, and an elastic modulus of 83.8 ± 13.4 kPa, closely resembling the properties of the healthy human cornea. In a rabbit model of deep corneal defects, the optimized in situ-forming hydrogel adapted to the defect geometry, adhered stably to the wound bed, recapitulated the optical and biomechanical properties of the native cornea, and supported scarless corneal stromal remodeling. Incorporation of the antimicrobial peptide HHC36 further endowed the hydrogel with robust antibacterial activity without compromising its optical and biomechanical properties. In a rabbit model of P. aeruginosa-infected deep corneal defects, the HHC36-loaded in situ-forming hydrogel effectively mitigated clinical signs of infection and substantially promoted corneal stromal remodeling within 30 days while reducing fibrosis. Overall, this optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched in situ dual-crosslinkable hydrogel might be a promising substitute for corneal stromal remodeling.

title: Improved Visualization of the Internal Branch of the Superior Laryngeal Nerve during Pharyngeal Endoscopic Subepithelial Dissection with Use of Red Dichromatic Imaging.
authors: Fujinaga Y, Tamada Y, Yamaguchi Y, Matsuura K, Kachi H, Oyama M, Mori H, Iwai S
abstract: Endoscopic subepithelial dissection is a minimally invasive treatment for superficial pharyngeal neoplastic lesions, requiring preservation of important neural structures such as the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (ibSLN). We report a case in which red dichromatic imaging (RDI) appeared to improve the visualization of a linear structure presumed to be the ibSLN compared with white-light imaging (WLI). A 57-year-old woman underwent endoscopic subepithelial dissection for a 5-mm superficial lesion on the pharyngoepiglottic fold. Both WLI and RDI revealed a whitish linear structure beneath the lesion, which was presumed to represent the ibSLN based on its anatomical location and course. The presumed nerve structure appeared to be more clearly delineated with RDI than with WLI before mucosal incision and remained identifiable after submucosal injection and during dissection. This enhanced visualization may have helped guide the selection of the mucosal incision line and dissection plane. En bloc resection was achieved without apparent nerve injury. No dysphagia, hoarseness, or other adverse events occurred postoperatively. These findings suggest that RDI may serve as a useful adjunct for visualization of the structure presumed to represent the ibSLN during pharyngeal endoscopic subepithelial dissection and may support nerve-preserving strategies.

A psychedelic-rich alkaloid fraction obtained from Mimosa tenuiflora (Willd.) Poir attenuates somatic and affective symptoms of naloxone-precipitated morphine withdrawal in C57BL/6 mice.
authors: da Silva TR, Machado KLB, Carvalho IMM, de Sousa DC, de M Campos FD, da Silva GO, da L de Oliveira GAM, de Sousa RP
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Mimosa tenuiflora (Willd.) Poir. root bark is traditionally used in northeastern Brazil to prepare "Jurema wine", a beverage employed to relieve emotional distress and restore psychological well-being. However, validating its traditional preparations in central substance withdrawal states remains underexplored. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the ethnopharmacological potential of M. tenuiflora, we investigated the effects of an alkaloid fraction (AF II) from its root bark on somatic and affective morphine withdrawal symptoms in mice, without compromising analgesia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Male C57BL/6 mice were used for the tests. Possible interference with morphine-induced analgesia was assessed using the acetic acid-induced writhing test. The animals were made morphine-dependent using a dose-escalation regimen, and withdrawal syndrome was precipitated with naloxone. AF II (3, 6, or 9 mg/kg, s.c.) was administered before withdrawal induction. RESULTS: AF II did not interfere with morphine analgesia. AF II significantly reduced key somatic signs of morphine withdrawal, decreasing jumping and paw tremor without affecting Walk in reverse. During withdrawal, AF II increased exploratory behavior in the open field and modulated anxiety-related parameters. CONCLUSIONS: The AF II from Mimosa tenuiflora, rich in serotonergic compounds, selectively attenuates somatic and affective components of opioid withdrawal in mice without compromising opioid analgesia, supporting its potential as a preliminary candidate for acute opioid withdrawal modulation. These findings provide scientific support for the traditional knowledge surrounding the central psychoactive and restorative properties of M. tenuiflora preparations.

title: Chaihu-Shugan-San attenuates depression by downregulating liver LCN2 to suppress LHb GluN2B-associated glutamatergic signaling.
authors: You X, Song C, Chen W, Zheng Y, Wang R, Liu W, Wei Y
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The liver-brain axis has emerged as a critical pathway in depression pathogenesis, yet the molecular basis of this crosstalk remains largely unexplored. Chaihu-Shugan-San (CSS), a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine formula for "soothing the liver and relieving depression" has shown both hepatoprotective and antidepressant effects, but whether these actions are linked via the liver-brain axis and through what molecular mechanism remains unknown. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to determine whether CSS exerts antidepressant effects via the liver-brain axis and to elucidate the mediating role of liver lipocalin 2 (LCN2) and its receptor SLC22A17 in regulating lateral habenula (LHb) function. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model was established. CSS (2, 4, 8 g/kg) or fluoxetine (10 mg/kg) was orally administered. Depressive-like behaviors were assessed by sucrose preference, open field, and forced swim tests. Hepatic injury was evaluated by serum ALT/AST and H&E staining. Liver transcriptomics and LHb single-cell RNA sequencing were performed to identify key molecules, followed by qRT-PCR, Western blot, ELISA, and immunofluorescence for validation. The causal role of LCN2 was tested via liver-specific AAV-mediated overexpression. RESULTS: CSS ameliorated CUMS-induced depressive-like behaviors and liver injury. Transcriptomics and PPI network analysis identified Lcn2 as a hub gene. CSS reversed CUMS-induced elevation of LCN2 in the liver, serum, and LHb, as well as the upregulation of its receptor SLC22A17 in the LHb. LHb single-cell sequencing revealed that CSS restored CUMS-induced changes in astrocyte subcluster ASC6, including downregulation of AQP4 and SLC38A1 and impaired intercellular communication. Consequently, CSS reduced the elevated expression of c-FOS and GluN2B and restored AQP4 and SLC38A1 in the LHb. Importantly, liver-specific Lcn2 overexpression recapitulated CUMS-like depressive phenotypes and LHb abnormalities, including elevated SLC22A17 and GluN2B, and largely abolished the antidepressant effects of CSS. CONCLUSION: CSS ameliorates depressive-like behaviors in association with downregulation of hepatic LCN2 and its candidate receptor SLC22A17 in the LHb, restoring ASC6-mediated glutamate homeostasis, and suppressing GluN2B-related Glutamatergic Signaling. These findings are consistent with a model in which LHb function may be modulated via the liver-brain axis through hepatic LCN2 and its candidate receptor SLC22A17, although the direct source of LHb LCN2 remains to be determined, offering experimental support for the scientific basis of CSS in "soothing the liver and relieving depression."

title: Label-free multi-metric pipeline for reproducible clustering of single-cell RNA-seq cell types.
authors: Yousef Z, Simone J, Klein D, Bhuyan A, Cho HJ, Bhatt P, Wu J, Wang H
abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has transformed our ability to identify cell types and explore cellular diversity. However, determining whether apparent cell subtypes represent true biological populations or artifacts of data analysis remains a major challenge. To address this issue, we developed scClustBench, an open-source benchmarking framework that evaluates cluster quality, stability, and reproducibility across multiple analytical approaches. Rather than relying on a single clustering method, scClustBench tests whether proposed cell subtypes can be consistently recovered. We applied scClustBench to a mouse retinal dataset containing bipolar cells, which are known to exhibit subtype diversity, and rod photoreceptors, for which subtype classification remains controversial. The framework consistently identified reproducible bipolar cell subtypes across analytical methods. In contrast, while some rod photoreceptor clusters appeared stable during resampling analyses, they could not be reproduced across embedding methods, suggesting that these partitions do not represent robust biological subtypes. Additional analyses using simulated and external datasets demonstrated that scClustBench reliably distinguishes meaningful cellular heterogeneity from analytical artifacts. These findings provide a practical framework for rigorous interpretation of single-cell transcriptomic data.

title: Type D personality, psychiatric symptom burden, and life satisfaction in bipolar II disorder and major depressive disorder: A family-based study.
authors: Örüm D, Örüm MH, Atmaca M
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type D personality combines negative affectivity (NA) and social inhibition (SI), yet its relevance to bipolar II disorder (BD-II), major depressive disorder (MDD), and their parents remains poorly understood. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 46 participants with BD-II and 46 with MDD in clinical remission, 50 controls without a current psychiatric disorder (C), and one co-residing biological parent per participant were assessed with the Type D Personality Scale (DS14), Adult Life Satisfaction Scale, Beck Depression Inventory-II, and clinician-rated Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS). NA, SI, and their interaction (NA × SI) were modelled continuously, with BPRS scores tested as a mediator of associations with life satisfaction. RESULTS: Type D personality was present in 87.0% of BD-II, 50.0% of MDD, and 10.0% of C participants (p < 0.001) and also differed across parental groups (fathers, p = 0.014; mothers, p = 0.030); pairwise differences from C parents were significant for fathers only. After covariate adjustment, participant groups differed in NA, SI, symptom burden, and life satisfaction (all Holm-corrected p < 0.001). In joint models, NA and SI were each associated with lower life satisfaction in all groups, whereas symptom burden was associated with NA in BD-II (p = 0.031) and SI in MDD (p = 0.004), but not in C participants, and not with NA × SI within any group. Corresponding indirect associations via symptom burden emerged in BD-II (NA: -0.653; BCa 95% CI: -1.610 to -0.155) and MDD (SI: -0.756; BCa 95% CI: -1.751 to -0.217), but not in C participants; the indirect effects did not differ significantly between BD-II and MDD. CONCLUSIONS: Within diagnostic groups, NA and SI, rather than their synergistic combination, were related to life satisfaction and, less consistently, symptom burden in remitted mood disorders; Type D characteristics were also elevated in parents.
